In Maestro, the price information is stored at a Part/Site/Customer, and Effective Date level. For products that don’t require order quantity-based pricing, the standard Customer Price table can be used to store and report the values.

docs.snippet: There are no exceptions as the idea is to standardize the S&OP process across all the BU’s.

docs.heading_path: Exceptions by Business Unit & Patch
docs.snippet:
Only the Part/Site which uses the Stocking Strategy as the Made To Stock (MTS) and Purchase To Stock (PTS) will use the safety and Cycle Stock.
For CAP plants, Safety Stock and Cycle Stock is not applicable. Only the Traded Packaged BU is using safety stock. But, in future, leveraging the safety stock depends on the business choice.

docs.heading_path: Exceptions by Business Unit & Patch
docs.snippet:
ChlorAlkali Caustic Manu Import – follows a slightly different supply planning process based on the supply planned on the Ship, it has a visibility of each ship arrival dates through the form of purchase order which will be created 3 weeks prior to the arrival. And the individual order lines contain information about how much it has to deliver against each delivery location (unload port).
Purchase Orders will be created 3 weeks prior to the due date of arrival. However, the primary focus remains on utilising the supply planning and order management functionality described above.

docs.heading_path: Exceptions by Business Unit & Patch
docs.snippet:
The ChlorAlkali Plants (CAP) in AU will use the Constraint Optimiser for short-term planning - covered in a separate blueprint document (IXOM Supply.AI Coproduct Optimization Solution Blueprint).
New Zealand Manufacturing

Though the Production Planners look at the Forecast for the production planning, their planning outcome will take into account the BLT Team distribution plan. Resource Mapping against the Demand Planning process steps

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
In addition to the Statistical Forecast, there are several external Forecasts that can be uploaded into Maestro for consideration when developing the Consensus Demand Plan.
You can upload, review and update external forecasts by choosing the Forecast Category, meaning that all the external forecast categories will be available by default in the workbook dropdown, depends on the forecast category selected the data will appear for review and modification. Similarly, the planner must choose the forecast category and then upload the forecast of that category. Please see examples of Forecast Catego

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
The Demand Planner/s and the Product Manager/s collectively review the demand volumes, (the system-generated Consensus Demand Plan based on assigned weightings) adjust or override the forecast for select products, if needed, and then approve the consensus demand/forecast. The final result is published and shared with the Supply Planners, as the Consensus Demand Plan (unconstrained demand plan).
Level 3 Processes: Consensus Demand Planning

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
The Demand Review is a meeting held once a month - typically in week 2 of every month. The purpose of this meeting is to align on the aggregated unconstrained Demand Plan, prioritise the decisions required, ensure decision statements are completed in preparation for the Demand Review and where the aggregate business plan lands compared to the budget, gain clear visibility of volume assumptions/risks & opportunities, and agree on recommendations for the Supply Review. The horizon of the plans considered in this process is 18-24 months.
L3 Process Flow – Demand Review
Ahead of the Demand Review

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
During the Supply Review process, the Production Planner & Supply Planner will review the Unconstrained Demand Plan from the Demand Review and compare it with the previous S&OP committed demand plan to understand the difference. Thereafter, the Production Planner & Supply Planner will review the Inventory position based on the Demand Plan and the existing On-Hand Stock & Firm Supply to identify the products where supply becomes available on a later date than the due date.
For production supplies, once the late supplies have been identified, the Production Planner will check the reason—whether

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
L3 Process Flow – Supply Review
The Supply Review meeting is between the Production Planner, Product Manager, Business Manager & Supply Planner to review the different option scenarios which have different supply plan, and to decide which scenarios to share with the Demand Planner as feedback/response.
The Supply Review meeting outputs are:
Best possible Production Plan & Supply Plan options
Feedback on Demand Review
Assumptions & gap closing action plans
The resources used to support this process are identified under the following topics:
Production & Material Planning
Supply Plan & Order Man

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet: In this process step, the Production Planners meet and discuss with the Supply Planners about the raw materials for production and then to Demand Planners for rebalancing the demand based on the production plan they come up with. And the Supply Planners will come up with the best possible Supply Plan and discuss with the Demand Planners. Thereafter, the Production Planners / Supply Planners will share an optimised production / supply plan and capture the assumptions. The Demand Planners will rebalance the demand to supply and capture if there are any new assumptions. The rebalanced demand plan

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
The purpose of this meeting is to agree and sign off on the business plan in volume and value for the next 18-24 months, make decisions on items escalated, raise recommendations from the earlier S&OP steps, review the financial projection of gaps identified during the reconciliation and agree on business choices for gap closing.
L3 Process Flow – Executive S&OP Meeting
The Process Overview meeting outputs:
Publish the approved S&OP plan in value/volume for the next 18-24 months
Clear actions and decisions from the recommendations/statements => feedback to the teams for the next Cycle

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
The Product Manager reviews and updates the ABC target percentages as needed. Based on these defined targets, the ABC classification is determined using the forecasted volume for the next 12 months and the calculated Gross Margin. Subsequently, an ABC Matrix will be applied, assigning a suggested ABC Code to each Part/Site. The Product Manager will then review these suggested classifications and make overrides if necessary.
Level 3 Process – ABC Classification

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
IXOM follows their own way of calculating the safety stock based on the defined service level, Mean Normal Deviation cap limits applied, lead time and the forecast. The Product Manager maintains the Service Level Target, MND Cap limits, and then based on the formula provided in Safety Stock Management, the Safety Stock will be calculated.
After Safety Stock is calculated, there is a concept of cycle stock which accumulates the demand within the delivery calendar and creates a single order to cover the whole demand i.e. cycle stock. At the end, the Product Manager reviews the Safety Stock and o

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
In this process step, the Product Manager reviews the Black Stock, adds the comments and captures the action plan to reduce the inventory. Similarly, the Product Manager reviews the SLOBS and formulates a resolution plan to reduce the inventory.
Level 3 Process – Black Stock & SLOBS

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
The Product Manager reviews and identifies the possible inventory transfer and creates the inventory movement to cover the shortfall with the existing inventory at other sites.
Level 3 Process – Inventory Transfer

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
This process involves the Supply Planner to review the existing Master data and update any information if changes required.
L3 Process Flow – Manage Planning Parameters

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
The Dispatcher works out a distribution plan by considering the consolidated demand coming from different medium and the logistics available such as Truck availability, driver’s availability, etc. The CAP plant Dispatcher Plans are brought into Maestro as Demand Orders and the system plans against that.
At each Part/Site (Delivery Location), Consensus Demand Plan (Forecast) gets consumed by the demand orders, if there is any unconsumed forecast exists, then system considers that in the Total Demand. After that if there are any safety stock requirements present, system makes sure the safety sto

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
Based on the system-suggested planned orders, the supply plan is evaluated to determine how effectively it meets the demand orders received from the Dispatcher.  Orders should be firmed when approaching the lead time or firming period, and existing firm orders can be updated in response to any changes in demand orders. Also, if there is any ad-hoc (non-regular) inventory transfer possible to fulfill the shortage at any location, inventory transfer can be created manually.
L3 Process – Constrain and Create Distribution Plan (Short-term)

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
The system takes the monthly forecast and the safety stock requirements, generates the long-term supply plan, from that you will understand the inventory projections throughout the planning horizon and do the rough-cut capacity planning.
Level 3 Process – Constrain and Create Distribution Plan (Short-term)

docs.snippet:
The Supply Planner reviews the input data received from ERP system and the data manually maintained in Maestro, if there are any changes required on the master data and on the pricing, Supply Planner will update it in the source system and the data flows onto the right scenario in Maestro.
Below are the level 3 process steps to Review and Update Master Data with its input and output provided.
Level 3 Process Flow – Review / Update Master Data

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
Once the master data has been reviewed and updated, based on the firmed/planned supply to satisfy the unconsumed forecast and the customer orders at the Finished Goods, the dependent demand will be exploded to the purchase parts or raw material in the BOM structure.
.  The Supply Planner reviews the dependent requirements to determine how much demand can be fulfilled based on available stock, how much can be satisfied through the firm supply plan, and how much the system will generate in planned orders. Also, whenever the inventory level goes below the safety stock, the system generates the su

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
In this process step, the Supply Planner will review the existing PReq/PO information and compare against the demand plan. When the system calculated planned orders enters the near-term horizon, the planner decides which one to convert it to firmed order by considering the safety stock and cycle stock, and the planner can release any PReq to SAP to get created in SAP system. Within SAP, the Supply Planner works with the Product Manager to convert the Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order.
Below is the process flow of updating the supply plan.
Level 3 Process Flow – Update Supply Plan

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
In the previous step, the supply planner updated the supply orders (or) created new firm orders (or) converted existing calculated planned orders to firm supply orders, depending on which inventory situation will be changed. So, the Supply planners will review the Parts where we have the inventory shortfall or excess inventory within the supply chain network.
In places where the shortfall exists, the root cause of the shortfall will be identified, and the supply planner will resolve the supply issues to the maximum extent possible and then also communicate with Demand Planner if the demand is

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
Once all the previous steps have been completed and the planner is happy with the supply plan and the resulting inventory projection and demand satisfaction, the Supply Planner releases the firmed Purchase Requisition from Maestro to SAP, by considering that as a signal SAP will create the PReq and send it back to Maestro. Additionally, the Product Manager can do the same in Maestro and he will convert the PReq to PO in SAP if necessary.
L3 Process Flow – Create PO and Update Supply Plan

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
The Production Planner reviews the existing Production related Master data and updates the information, if changes are required.
Level 3 Process Flow – Maintain Planning Parameters
Note: Master data will come from SAP. If the Planner modifies the data in Maestro, the modified data will persist until a data change comes from the ERP system. If the data needs to be modified in ERP system, the Planner/authorised user can update it in the ERP system and it will flow to Maestro.

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
In this process, the Production Planner reviews the effective total demand, determines the source of the demand, reviews the any supply imbalances vs. demand, creates new process orders, updates existing process orders and reviews the inventory projection to make sure there is no shortfall. The Production Planner then creates a production plan to fulfill the demand - all within Maestro.
Level 3 Process – Create Initial Version Of Production Plan
Note : In AU for manufacturing sites that use process orders, the process orders are created by the site leaders or operators. Some site leaders do pl

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
In this Level 3 process, the Production Planner will review the supply imbalances to demand and rectify the imbalances. Thereafter, Maestro checks the Process Order availability and identifies late orders. Once the late orders have been identified, the production planner will analyse the reason for lateness, either within the material or the manufacturing constraint.
If the lateness is due to a Manufacturing Constraint, the Production Planner needs to resolve the capacity constraint related issues, or find an alternate source to resolve the issue. If the lateness is due to material availabilit

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
In this Level 3 process flow, the Production Planner updates the existing Process orders and creates any new firm process orders after collaborating with the Supply Planner. They then review the inventory projection, and the production planner submits the Production Plan to the Product Manager. The Product Manager reviews/updates the final Production Plan and release it as the confirmed/live plan. The individual responsibilities will be confirmed during implementation.
Level 3 Process – Finalise & Release Production Plan
Note: This step is not applicable for NZ.  Currently in AU process orders

docs.heading_path: Process Overview
docs.snippet:
The RCCP process, utilises the long-term monthly forecast to generate the required planned orders. The Production Planner then reviews and identifies inventory issues, imbalances between supply and demand, gating constraints and material constraints. The Production Planner then attempts to resolve the issues identified. If unable to do so, the Production Planner will capture all assumptions and submit the best possible production plan to the Product Manager.
Again, the individual responsibilities will be confirmed during implementation.
